technical_and_design_decisions: Single developer will personally implement all work; no team coordination overhead is included beyond what is intrinsic to each task.
Development will leverage the existing Spring XD codebase, build system (Gradle/Maven), and test infrastructure.

For U7 (Module deployment SPI migration), the existing 'repository' abstraction will be replaced by a Java SPI interface, keeping the legacy repository as the default implementation to preserve backward compatibility.
For U8 (Boot-based ModuleRunner), Spring Boot will be used as the runtime foundation; the ModuleRunner will be packaged as an executable JAR suitable for containerized deployment.
For U4 and U5 (benchmarks), JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness) will be used as the primary benchmarking framework to ensure statistically meaningful results.
For U6 (GPDB parameter UX), a quoting/escaping abstraction layer will be introduced to hide database-specific syntax from end users.
For U3 (XD+Kafka POC), the sample will follow the existing Spring XD samples repository conventions (Maven modules, README-driven documentation).
All CI changes (U2) will target the existing CI server (Jenkins) configuration, using a declarative pipeline or job DSL approach.
Code reviews are assumed to be handled by peers asynchronously; the estimates include minor rework time but not a full review cycle.
assumptions: The developer is already familiar with the Spring XD codebase, so no significant ramp-up is required beyond 1 day of environment verification.
External systems required for testing (Kafka cluster, GPDB instance, SQLServer instance, Hadoop/HDFS) are provisioned and reachable from the development environment.
The 'remaining work' for the DEBS challenge (U1) is estimated as a moderate-sized implementation (approx. 3 days) plus testing and submission overhead; this is a best-guess since the spec is vague.
No major architectural discoveries or new platform requirements are expected during implementation; estimates reflect a smooth development path.
The XD + Kafka POC (U3) targets a working reference implementation with documentation, not a production-grade system.
Performance optimization work in U4 and U5 assumes that 1–2 concrete optimizations will be implemented and verified, not a full overhaul.
The pluggable runtime SPI (U7) will not require changes to existing stream/job definition APIs, only to the deployment layer.
Container-managed environment testing in U8 will use a locally available container runtime (e.g., Docker) without requiring cloud provisioning.
